fact: The Minister for Lands said the Lands Commission's ongoing ELIS digitization would eliminate manual inefficiencies, and the article says full migration from manual operations is still in progress.
The article says ELIS remains the backbone of the Lands Commission's online services, with manual processes coexisting, and progress is anchored largely in Accra.
Then-Lands Minister Jinapor acknowledged that ELIS had enabled consolidated searches, stamp duty assessment and plan approvals to be completed online.
A digital Client Service Access Unit inaugurated at the Volta Regional Lands Commission office in Ho enabled the deployment of ELIS in the Volta Region.

Ghana News Agency quotes the Lands Commission's Executive Secretary saying ELIS, its digital land platform, is operational in Greater Accra and nine other regions, with nationwide rollout targeted for end-2027.
Graphic Online reports that on 15 July 2026 the Lands Minister said the Enterprise Land Information System is operational in nine of the Lands Commission's regional offices.

Graphic Online reports that on 15 July 2026 the Lands Minister said the public can apply online for official land searches in the nine regions where the Enterprise Land Information System is operational.

The Lands Commission says it has scanned, geo-referenced and digitised existing records and runs them on ELIS, cutting file retrieval from months to a few days, and lists national roll-out as still to come.
The Lands Commission's online portal lets applicants submit and track searches and registration, including first registration and transfers, and pay online.

Ghana News Agency reports that on 2 September 2025 President Mahama tasked the Lands Commission to digitise all land records nationwide, building on the enterprise land information system, and to open land offices in all 261 district assemblies.
The Lands Commission says its Enterprise Land Information System provides registration and searches, in use now.
Dr Benjamin Quaye says industry players can now conduct land searches online through the Enterprise Land Information System without visiting the Commission.
Graphic Online reports Vice President Bawumia citing digitised land title certificates at the Lands Commission on 25 November 2024.
Graphic Online reports the Lands Commission's online searches and consolidated search process, praised by the Vice President on 25 November 2024.
